name: Beta-thalassemia associated with another hemoglobin anomaly
aliases: Compound beta-thalassemia and hemoglobin variant disorder

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutations in the HBB gene and coexisting hemoglobin variant gene
Abnormal hemoglobin electrophoresis showing reduced or absent HbA with presence of abnormal hemoglobin variant
Presence of anemia with microcytosis and clinical signs consistent with thalassemia or hemoglobinopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of beta-thalassemia mutation plus identification of another hemoglobin anomaly by electrophoresis or molecular testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, hematological, and clinical data due to phenotypic variability.

laboratory: Reduced hemoglobin A levels with presence of abnormal hemoglobin variants
Microcytic hypochromic anemia with elevated reticulocyte count
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation in iron overload
imaging: Bone marrow expansion visible on skull and long bone X-rays
Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
Cardiac MRI showing iron deposition in myocardium
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in HBB gene causing beta-thalassemia
Coexisting mutations in globin genes encoding abnormal hemoglobin variants (e.g., HbS, HbC, HbE)
other: Hemoglobin electrophoresis and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) for hemoglobin variant identification

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of coexisting abnormal hemoglobin variants
Presence of HbS without beta-thalassemia mutations
Characteristic sickling of red blood cells

redFlags: Signs of iron overload such as cardiac or hepatic dysfunction
